questions.question: How are night terrors (pavor nocturnus) distinguished from nightmares?

options.A: Night terrors occur during REM sleep and are clearly remembered; nightmares occur during NREM sleep and are forgotten
options.B: Night terrors occur during Stage 4 NREM sleep early in the night with complete amnesia; nightmares occur during REM sleep, usually later in the night, and are clearly remembered
options.C: There is no real difference between the two conditions
options.D: Both occur exclusively in adults, never in children

questions.explanation: Night terrors are a Stage 4 NREM parasomnia occurring in the first third of the night, with autonomic arousal (tachycardia, sweating) and complete amnesia for the event on waking. Nightmares, by contrast, occur during REM sleep (more common in the last third of the night) and are vividly and clearly remembered.

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient diagnosed with an acute posterior cruciate sprain. The mechanism of injury for the posterior cruciate is:
